slots_and_copies.name: header_block
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: FUN_0807cb60 calls FUN_0807cc34(0); if it returns 0 (checksum + build-tag + complement all valid) this block is treated as the active header.

slots_and_copies.name: candidate_slot_b
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: FUN_0807cc34(1) validates a second 128-byte candidate at base+0x80 (in words). No populated copy was observed at SRAM offset 0x80-0xFF in either .sav (both are 0xFF fill), so it is unresolved whether this candidate is ever physically written to this SRAM offset or is RAM-only.

slots_and_copies.name: unresolved_zero_block
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Zero-filled in both captures; no decompiled function references absolute SRAM offset 0x100. FUN_08000e50 reads 0x00-0xFF, not this range.

slots_and_copies.name: footer_tag
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Static 'METDSAVE\0\0' tag followed by 0xFF fill; identical in both captures; no writer or reader traced in available decompilation.

checksums.name: header_block_sum32_complement
checksums.formula_detail: Sum of all 32 little-endian u32 words of SRAM 0x00-0x7F, with word0 forced to 0x00000000 and word1 forced to 0xFFFFFFFF before summing. Result stored at offset 0x00; one's complement (~sum) stored at offset 0x04. Validator additionally checks stored_sum == ~stored_complement.

io_driver_functions.notes: Full-SRAM writer: stages RAM mirror via func_0x080030a0 then flushes 0x8000 bytes to 0xe000000 via func_0x08004dc8.
Writes just the 128-byte checksummed header block to 0xe000000 via func_0x08004dc8.
Reads 256 bytes (0x00-0xFF) from 0xe000000 into RAM via func_0x08004c90.
Serializes header fields (tag bytes, build string) and computes/stores the sum32/complement checksum pair, then calls 0x08000dac.
Validator: recomputes sum32, compares build-tag bytes, checks sum/complement self-consistency; returns a 3-bit failure mask.
SRAM presence self-test: writes 16 bytes, reads back, increments, rewrites, and compares to detect whether save hardware is present/writable.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Top-level save-menu/dispatch entry point; no static caller recovered in ghidra/callgraph.json (reached via an un-recovered indirect jump table at 0x0807cae4/0x0807cc2c).
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced via ghidra/callgraph.json caller/callee edges starting from the three literal 0xe000000 MMIO seed call sites in ghidra/save_related_functions.c, then cross-referenced against ghidra/decompiled.c for full function bodies.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Called at the end of FUN_0807cb60's save-due branch, immediately after the full-SRAM write (0x08000d74), to (re)serialize and flush the 128-byte header with a freshly computed checksum.
caller_chains.how_mapped: ghidra/callgraph.json: "0x08000dac": {"callers": ["0x0807caf4", "0x0807cb60"]} combined with decompiled.c body of FUN_0807caf4.

fields.name: header_checksum_sum32
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed on every header serialization as the sum of all 32 header words (with this word and the complement word forced to placeholder values first).
fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body; Python re-derivation matches both .sav files exactly (see SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.2).

fields.name: header_checksum_complement
fields.update_mechanism: Stored as the bitwise one's complement of the sum32 at offset 0, so sum+complement always equals 0xFFFFFFFF.
fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body; Python verification: (stored_sum + stored_complement) & 0xFFFFFFFF == 0xFFFFFFFF on both files.

fields.name: tag_char_0
fields.update_mechanism: Literal immediate store of '0' on every header serialization.
fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body, line *(undefined1*)(_DAT_0807cb54+2)=0x30; byte matches both .sav files.

fields.name: tag_char_1
fields.update_mechanism: Literal immediate store of '1' on every header serialization.
fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body; byte matches both .sav files.

fields.name: unresolved_global_byte

fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body; source global not further resolvable in available decompilation.

fields.name: constant_flag_byte

fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 decompiled body; byte matches both .sav files.

fields.name: build_tag_string
fields.update_mechanism: 20-byte copy loop from a fixed source (_DAT_0807cb5c) on every header serialization; compared byte-for-byte on validation against a fixed reference (_DAT_0807cca4).
fields.evidence: FUN_0807caf4 copy loop and FUN_0807cc34 compare loop both decompiled; string matches both .sav files exactly.

fields.name: header_reserved_padding
fields.update_mechanism: Not individually written by any traced function; swept into the checksum sum as part of the 128-byte block loop.
fields.evidence: Byte range verified as 0xFF fill in both .sav files; no writer found in ghidra/decompiled.c.

fields.name: candidate_slot_b_bytes
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; validated by FUN_0807cc34(1) but never observed populated on disk in either capture.
fields.evidence: FUN_0807cc34 validates a second 128-byte candidate at base+0x80 words; SRAM offset 0x80-0xFF is 0xFF fill (unpopulated) in both .sav files.

fields.name: unresolved_zero_block
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; no decompiled function references absolute SRAM offset 0x100.

fields.name: volatile_counter_bytes
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; changed between the two captures but no writer traced.
fields.evidence: Byte-diff between cap-00 and cap-01 at 0x7040-0x7044; not ASCII, not matching the sum/complement checksum shape used elsewhere.

fields.name: unexplained_language_key_text
fields.update_mechanism: Text absent from ghidra/decompiled.c entirely; hypothesized to be uninitialized RAM-mirror content leaked through the full-32KiB bulk writer (0x08000d74) rather than a deliberately written field.
fields.evidence: saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt diff between the two capture files; string searched for and not found anywhere in ghidra/decompiled.c.

fields.name: footer_tag_string
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; identical across both captures, but no writer or reader for this string exists in the available decompilation.
fields.evidence: Bytes proven identical in both .sav files via direct Python read; no matching function found in ghidra/decompiled.c.

fields.name: footer_fill
fields.update_mechanism: Erased-SRAM default, trailing the footer tag.
fields.evidence: Byte range verified as 0xFF fill in both .sav files.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: increment one byte of the stored sum32 without updating the complement
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_0807cc34(0) sets failure bit 0x1 on next boot; slot-selection logic should treat the header as invalid.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one byte inside the AGBMetroid_USVerE003 build tag, then repair the sum32/complement pair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Checksum check passes (bit 0x1 clear) but build-tag compare fails (bit 0x2 set), isolating whether the tag is independently enforced.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set the complement word to a value that is not ~sum, while leaving the sum itself internally correct
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Sum recompute still matches (bit 0x1 clear) but self-consistency bit 0x4 sets, proving the two checks are independent.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: zero the 0x7040-0x7066 region after it has been populated (as in cap-01), then replay identical frame count under emulation
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is leaked uninitialized data (hypothesis), repeated identical play sessions will NOT reliably reproduce the same bytes here; if it is a real field, the same bytes should reappear deterministically.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: fill 0x100-0x1FF with a non-zero marker pattern and reload
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Pattern should persist unchanged across a boot/save cycle, since no traced reader/writer touches this absolute offset; any change would reveal an untraced function.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip the first byte of the METDSAVE footer tag
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Unknown by design; no reader was traced for this tag, so this test is purely exploratory to discover whether any boot path depends on it.

open_questions: Who calls FUN_0807cb60? No caller edge exists in ghidra/callgraph.json; the indirect jump table at 0x0807cae4/0x0807cc2c could not be recovered.
What RAM-absolute addresses do _DAT_0807cbbc/_DAT_0807cbb8/_DAT_0807cbc0/_DAT_0807cbc4/_DAT_0807cbc8 refer to, and do they correspond to real in-RAM save-struct mirrors at 0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx?
Is there a genuine second physical 128-byte header slot anywhere in the 32 KiB SRAM, or is FUN_0807cc34(1)'s second candidate purely a RAM-resident template never materialized to disk?
What writes the METDSAVE tag at 0x7FF0, and is it ever read back by any code path?
Is the 0x7040 text block ('fSTARTKEYLANGUAGE'/'ENDKEY_LANGUAGE_') genuine leaked Beta-build debug content, or an as-yet-unidentified real save field?
What (untraced) code clears SRAM 0x100-0x1FF to zero, and why does it differ from the 0xFF fill used everywhere else on this cart?
